Continuous-length seals, channels and structural profiles extruded to drawing at our ISO 9001:2015 certified plant in Nashik, India. Five compounds, eight standard sections, and per-metre pricing quoted against your total run length.

Clean 2D cross-section drawings — every profile is available in any compound from the specification table below. Dimensional conformity to ISO 3302-1, class E1 to E3 as recorded on the drawing; ±0.2 mm held on critical dimensions, with the tolerance on any one dimension set by the section rather than applied across the profile.
Every compound blended in-house. Five polymers covering −60 °C to +250 °C and the full chemical exposure spectrum.

Hardness and temperature ranges are stated as standard blends; custom formulations available on request. Extrusion hardness bands are narrower than our moulding range on purpose — a profile has to hold its section coming off the die and through cure, which rules out the softest and hardest ends. Natural rubber, SBR and AEM are available on extruded profiles to order and are not part of the standard library. All compounds tested to the ISO and ASTM methods listed in the quality section below.

Quality That Travels With Every Metre

Every production batch is tested for hardness, tensile strength and compression set before despatch, and the results travel with the delivery. Compound qualification tests — ozone, heat ageing and low-temperature flexibility — are run once per formulation through our NABL-accredited partner laboratory and issued on request. Reports are supplied as standard with export orders.
Every metre we ship carries a batch test certificate. You never have to ask — it arrives with the delivery note, before you even open the box.

From construction curtain wall to industrial fluid systems — our extrusions solve the same fundamental sealing problem across every sector. Each card links to the industry page for the parts we make alongside the profile.

Extrusion is priced by the metre rather than by the piece, so a run is quoted against total length, section complexity and compound. Minimum run is quoted per profile against total length, because a thin cord and a large hollow section are not the same job.
